summary: Genuinely mutual NDA on Ballybrick paper that largely tracks the playbook, with a heightened evidence standard for carve-outs, a 'forthwith' return obligation, no insurers in Representatives, a Purpose-agnostic definition and an uncovered breach-notification duty.

findings.quote: In consideration of the mutual disclosure of Confidential Information hereunder, the Receiving Party hereby covenants, warrants and agrees with the Disclosing Party that it shall:
findings.why: Obligations bind the Receiving Party and Disclosing Party and Receiving Party are defined by role, so either party can be either.

findings.quote: disclosed or made available by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party to the Receiving Party, whether before, on or after the date hereof
findings.why: The definition is not tied to information disclosed for the Permitted Purpose and reaches information disclosed before the agreement date, although it does cover marked or reasonably confidential information and derived notes.
findings.draft_redline: "Confidential Information" means all information disclosed or made available by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party to the Receiving Party for the Permitted Purpose, whether before, on or after the date hereof, which is marked as confidential or which would reasonably be considered confidential, together with all analyses, compilations, notes and other records prepared by the Receiving Party containing or reflecting such information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like the definition to be tied to information disclosed for the Permitted Purpose. Otherwise we are content with its scope.

findings.quote: solely and exclusively for the Permitted Purpose, and under no circumstances utilise the same for its own commercial benefit or for any other purpose whatsoever
findings.why: Use is limited to the Permitted Purpose, being discussions on a prospective distribution, reselling and integration transaction, which is a named commercial evaluation.

findings.quote: which the Receiving Party can conclusively demonstrate by contemporaneous documentary evidence
findings.why: All four carve-outs are present, but they apply only if proved conclusively by contemporaneous documentary evidence, which is stricter than the 'written records' or 'reasonable evidence' standard in the playbook.
findings.draft_redline: 4.1 The covenants, undertakings and restrictions set out in Clause 2 shall not apply to any Information which the Receiving Party can demonstrate by written records or other reasonable evidence:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are happy with the four standard exclusions but would ask that the evidence standard be 'written records or other reasonable evidence' rather than conclusive contemporaneous documentary evidence.

findings.quote: only to such of its Representatives and Affiliates who have a clear and demonstrable need to know
findings.why: Directors, officers, employees, advisers, auditors and Affiliates are covered on a need-to-know basis with liability for them, but the Representatives definition in 1.1.8 does not include insurers.
findings.draft_redline: 1.1.8 "Representatives" means the directors, officers, employees, professional legal advisers, accountants, auditors, insurers and corporate consultants of a Party or of its Affiliates.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Please could insurers be added to the list of Representatives, as we may need to share information with them on a need-to-know basis.

findings.quote: to the extent legally permissible, it shall:
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted to the extent required, with notice only where legally permissible and cooperation in opposing disclosure at the Disclosing Party's expense.

findings.quote: upon the written demand of the Disclosing Party at any time, or forthwith upon the termination or expiry of this Agreement
findings.why: Return or destruction is due 'forthwith' on termination, which is shorter than the 5 Business Day minimum, although the officer certificate (14 days) and backup and legal-retention exceptions in 6.2 are acceptable.
findings.draft_redline: 6.1 Subject to Clause 6.2, within ten (10) Business Days of the written request of the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party shall:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would ask for a fixed period of ten Business Days for return or destruction rather than 'forthwith'. The backup and legal-retention exception in 6.2 is fine.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information, including all intellectual property rights therein, shall remain the sole, absolute and exclusive property of the Disclosing Party and its licensors.
findings.why: Ownership stays with the Disclosing Party and no licence is granted to the Receiving Party.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information is provided by the Disclosing Party on an "as is" basis without warranty of any kind.
findings.why: Mutual as-is and no-warranty disclaimer, with a no-obligation-to-proceed statement in 7.3 and no liability exclusion removing a fraud carve-out.

findings.quote: Neither Party shall make, issue or authorise any press release, public statement, advertisement or marketing announcement concerning the existence, subject matter, terms or negotiations of this Agreement
findings.why: Mutual publicity restriction requiring prior written approval, though it lacks an express exception for disclosures required by law (covered by clause 5.1).
findings.fallback_cited: Mutual publicity restriction in any reasonable wording.

findings.quote: the Disclosing Party shall be entitled, in addition to any other rights or remedies available to it at law or in equity, to seek and obtain injunctive relief, specific performance and any other form of equitable remedy
findings.why: Equitable relief is available to whichever party is the Disclosing Party and remedies are cumulative; it is strongly worded and waives any bond but is mutual.
findings.fallback_cited: Strongly worded but mutual equitable relief.

findings.quote: initial term of two (2) years, subject to the right of either Party to terminate this Agreement at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: Two-year term with 30 days' notice to terminate early.

findings.quote: shall survive and continue to bind the Receiving Party for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of such termination or expiration, save that in respect of any Information which constitutes a trade secret, such obligations shall endure for so long as the relevant Information retains the character of a trade secret
findings.why: Confidentiality survives three years after termination or expiry, with trade secrets protected for as long as they remain trade secrets.

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign, transfer, charge, sub-contract or delegate any of its rights, benefits or burdens under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party, save that either Party may assign this Agreement to an Affiliate or to a successor in title
findings.why: Mutual consent requirement with a mutual carve-out for Affiliates and successors, although the carve-out does not expressly require notice.
findings.fallback_cited: Either party may assign to a Group member or successor on notice.

findings.quote: refrain from reverse engineering, decompiling, disassembling, probing, translating or otherwise attempting to reconstruct or discover any underlying algorithms, protocols, source code or architectural blueprints
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and technical artifacts furnished by the Disclosing Party is prohibited.

findings.quote: shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of England and Wales.
findings.why: English law governs, and clause 10.11 gives the courts of England and Wales exclusive jurisdiction.

findings.quote: shall forthwith notify the Disclosing Party in writing upon discovering or suspecting any unauthorised use, disclosure, dissemination or loss of any Confidential Information, and shall, at its own expense, co-operate fully with the Disclosing Party in taking all reasonable steps to recover the information
findings.why: This breach-notification and recovery-cooperation duty at the Receiving Party's own cost is not covered by any playbook rule, so a lawyer should confirm it.
